subject: Career
title: The Stanford Remote Work Experiment
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Stanford Remote Work Experiment.

hook.text: Nick Bloom ran the first rigorous remote work experiment. The results shocked the business world.

buildup.text: In 2013, Ctrip let half its call center work from home. Performance jumped 13%.

discovery.text: Remote workers took fewer breaks, had fewer sick days, and reported higher job satisfaction.

twist.text: But 50% of home workers eventually chose to return. Loneliness and career invisibility were the reasons.

climax.text: The experiment proved remote work boosts productivity but requires solving isolation and visibility.

punchline.text: Remote work works. But it works best with intentional design.

quiz.question: What did Nick Bloom's Stanford experiment find about remote work?
options: Performance increased 13% but loneliness was a challenge

details.summary: Stanford professor Nicholas Bloom's 2015 study of a Chinese travel agency found that remote workers were thirteen percent more productive, took fewer sick days, and reported higher satisfaction. It became the most cited academic evidence for remote work effectiveness.
details.whyItMatters: This randomized controlled trial provided rigorous scientific evidence that remote work boosts productivity, giving advocates concrete data to counter skeptics' claims.
takeaways: Remote workers showed a thirteen percent productivity increase in the study
Fewer sick days and breaks contributed to the productivity gains
About half the gain came from a quieter working environment

faq.question: Can the Stanford remote work study results be generalized to all industries?
faq.answer: The study involved call center workers, so direct generalization requires caution. However, subsequent studies across multiple industries have replicated the finding that focused individual work benefits from remote settings. Collaborative and creative work shows more mixed results.

faq.question: What were the limitations of the Stanford remote work experiment?
faq.answer: The study was limited to one company, one culture, and one type of work. It was also conducted with volunteers, which introduces self-selection bias. Workers who chose remote work may have been predisposed to thrive in that environment, unlike a mandated remote policy.
